Contributing to koine

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Thanks for your interest in koine. The package is in early development; the notes below keep contributions consistent with the house conventions.

Workflow

  • Branch off main: feature/<short-name> or bugfix/<short-name>. Merge back to main only after the checks pass.
  • Keep commits small and focused, and explain why in the message (e.g. “address #2 – reconstruct pointwise log-likelihood via the family spec”, not “minor change”).
  • A pull request that closes an issue must say so in its body: Fixes #<n>.

Quality gates

Before opening a pull request:

devtools::document()
devtools::test()                       # all green
rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck(args = "--as-cran")  # zero ERRORs / WARNINGs
  • Add a NEWS.md bullet for any user-facing change.
  • New or changed code follows the two-space / 80-character house style; the repository carries an air.toml so Air agrees with it. Do not restyle code unrelated to your change.
  • Document every exported function with roxygen2 (markdown), including a runnable @examples block.

Validating a new lens

A koine-authored lens must clear the correctness gate before it may contribute to triangulation: simulation-based calibration and a reference-posterior check (see inst/validation/ and koine_lens_validation_setup()). Wire the lens’s generative model into the validation harness, run the study, record the verdict, and attach the resulting validation_ref in the registry. An unvalidated lens must abstain – it is never silently trusted.
